match.reason: The closest bank point, Connotation and denotation, covers the similar-meaning, different-connotation idea but not its link to tone or how the reader judges a moment, and the tone-focused cards teach tone as the writer's attitude rather than word choice, so no bank point matches this point exactly.

draft.title: Choosing words for tone
card: A word has a denotation, its basic dictionary meaning. It also has connotations, the feelings and ideas that come with it.
Words with similar meanings can carry different connotations. Scolded, criticised and attacked all describe someone speaking against another person, but they do not feel the same.
Scolded sounds like a parent or teacher correcting a child. Criticised sounds calm and fair. Attacked sounds harsh and aggressive.
The word a writer picks sets the tone, which is the attitude a text takes. It also shapes how the reader judges the people and events in the moment.
draft.remember: Similar words are not the same: each connotation changes the tone and how a reader judges.

a.q: Which word choice makes the coach sound most aggressive and hostile? The coach ___ the referee after the match.
a.why: Attacked carries connotations of violence and hostility, so the coach seems aggressive. Corrected is the most tempting wrong option, but it sounds calm and neutral, as if the coach were simply fixing a mistake.
a.clue: Which word sounds like a fight?

b.q: A writer wants readers to see Mia as fair and reasonable when she speaks about her team's weak effort. Which sentence best does this?
opts: Mia criticised the team's effort at training
Mia savaged the team's effort at training
Mia lectured the team about its effort at training
Mia scolded the team like children at training
b.why: Criticised has a calm, measured tone, so Mia seems fair. Lectured is the most tempting wrong option, but it suggests she talked at length in a preachy way, which makes readers judge her less kindly. Savaged and scolded sound harsh or talk down to the team.
b.clue: Look for the word with the calmest connotation.

b.best: Mia criticised the team's effort at training
